scenes.narration: [serious] One small free tool put hundreds of millions of devices in danger.
The tool was called Log4j. It keeps a diary for apps. Volunteers built it. Thousands of apps use it.
In November 2021, a worker at Alibaba found a hole in it. They quietly warned the volunteers.
In December, the problem went public. Even Minecraft rushed out a fix.

visuals.text: Huge hole found in free tool

scenes.narration: America's top cyber official called it one of the worst problems she had ever seen.
Here's the twist. No single company was hacked. The weak spot was inside apps everywhere.
Officials warned it could last ten years or more. Much of the internet runs on volunteers' work.

facts.claim: Log4j is a free, open-source Java logging library created by Apache Software Foundation volunteers; a member of Alibaba's cloud security team found the flaw and Apache was alerted on November 24
U.S. officials estimated hundreds of millions of devices were exposed; Minecraft's makers warned players and released a patch
CISA director Jen Easterly called the flaw one of the most serious she has seen in her entire career, if not the most serious; tracked as CVE-2021-44228

The Cyber Safety Review Board (July 2022) called Log4j an endemic vulnerability that may remain for a decade or longer; Log4j is in thousands of software packages and is maintained by a volunteer-led community

seo.title: Log4Shell: The Free Tool That Put Millions of Devices at Risk
seo.description: In December 2021 a flaw in Log4j, a free logging tool built by volunteers, exposed hundreds of millions of devices.
